tasks.title: Add rate limiting and input sanitization to API endpoints
tasks.description: Implement a request‑rate‑limiting middleware (e.g., express‑rate‑limit) in server.js to protect public endpoints from brute‑force and DoS attacks. Add a validation layer using a schema library (e.g., Joi) in src/lib/db.js and route handlers to sanitize and validate all incoming parameters (search queries, booking dates, user IDs). This prevents injection attacks and ensures only well‑formed data reaches the database.
acceptance: Requests exceeding 100 per minute from the same IP receive HTTP 429 responses.
All API payloads are validated against defined Joi schemas; malformed requests return HTTP 400 with a clear error message.
No SQL injection or XSS payload can be persisted in the database (verified with automated security tests).

tasks.title: Introduce DB connection pooling and in‑memory caching for listings
tasks.description: Refactor src/lib/db.js to use a connection pool (e.g., pg‑pool for PostgreSQL) instead of creating a new client per request, reducing latency and resource usage. Add a simple LRU cache (e.g., node‑cache) for the most‑requested listings (GET /listings) and search results, with a TTL of 5 minutes. Update server.js to serve cached data when available and fall back to the DB otherwise.
acceptance: Database connections are reused; the number of active connections never exceeds the pool size (e.g., 20).
Cache hit rate for listings is at least 60% in load tests.
Response time for GET /listings drops by ≥30% compared to baseline (measured with a simple load test).

tasks.title: Add CSRF protection to state‑changing endpoints
tasks.description: Integrate the existing csrfMiddleware into the Express pipeline for all POST/PUT/DELETE routes (including /graphql). Generate a CSRF token on authentication, store it in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, and require the token in the 'x-csrf-token' header. Reject requests missing or with an invalid token with 403. Update authMiddleware to set the cookie flags (secure in production, httpOnly, sameSite).
acceptance: A CSRF token is set as a cookie after login and can be read via generateCsrfToken()
POST/PUT/DELETE requests without the x-csrf-token header are responded with 403
Valid token requests succeed and the cookie has HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure (in prod) flags

tasks.title: Enforce strict input validation and sanitization for listings and bookings
tasks.description: Use the existing Joi schemas (listingSchema, bookingSchema) in the request handlers for creating/updating listings and bookings. Replace the simple HTML regex strip with a robust library (e.g., DOMPurify) to prevent XSS, and enforce length limits on strings. Return 400 with clear error messages on validation failure.
acceptance: Creating or updating a listing with HTML tags results in stripped content, not stored raw
Requests with missing required fields or invalid types are rejected with 400 and a Joi error message
All mutation endpoints (e.g., insertListing, insertBooking) now validate payloads before DB insertion

tasks.title: Set secure cookie attributes for auth tokens
tasks.description: Configure the authentication cookie to include HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict flags. Update the token generation logic in src/lib/auth.js and the cookie middleware in server.js to use these options. This prevents client‑side script access and mitigates CSRF and session hijacking attacks.
acceptance: Set‑Cookie header contains HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict for all authentication cookies
Browser devtools show the cookie as inaccessible to JavaScript
Existing login flow works without errors after the change

tasks.title: Enforce CSRF token validation on all state‑changing endpoints
tasks.description: Apply the csrfMiddleware to every POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE route (including GraphQL mutations) and ensure a token is generated and sent via the X‑CSRF‑Token header. Update the client to read the token from the response header and include it in subsequent mutating requests.
acceptance: Missing or invalid X‑CSRF‑Token header results in 403 response
Successful mutating request includes a valid token and returns 200/201 as expected
Integration test verifies that a POST request without the token is rejected

tasks.title: Add Content Security Policy header
tasks.description: Configure Helmet to include a strict Content Security Policy that allows scripts, styles, images and fonts only from trusted origins, blocks inline execution, and reports violations. This mitigates XSS and data injection attacks across the entire application.
acceptance: Response headers contain a CSP header with directives disallowing 'unsafe-inline' and restricting sources to self and approved CDNs
Automated security scan (e.g., npm audit, OWASP ZAP) reports no CSP-related vulnerabilities
Manual testing of a page with injected script tags results in the script being blocked

tasks.title: Enforce HTTP Strict Transport Security
tasks.description: Add the Strict-Transport-Security header via Helmet to force browsers to use HTTPS for all future requests, include subdomains and the preload flag. This protects against protocol downgrade attacks and cookie hijacking.
acceptance: All HTTPS responses include the 'Strict-Transport-Security' header with max-age>=31536000, includeSubDomains, and preload
Curl request to https endpoint returns the HSTS header
Browser console shows no mixed‑content warnings after enabling HSTS

tasks.title: Migrate all DB access to prepared statements
tasks.description: Replace any raw string concatenation used in `src/lib/db.js` with parameterized queries using `better-sqlite3`'s `prepare`, `run`, `get`, and `all` methods. Ensure every function that interacts with the database (e.g., insertListing, updateBookingStatus, getUserByEmail, etc.) uses bound parameters to prevent SQL injection and improve query planning. Add unit tests that attempt injection payloads and verify they are safely escaped.
acceptance: All DB functions use `db.prepare(...).run(...)` or `.get(...)` with placeholders
Injection attempts (e.g., "' OR 1=1 --") are rejected or result in no data leakage
Existing functionality (CRUD operations) continues to work as before

tasks.title: Add GraphQL query depth limiting
tasks.description: Integrate a depth‑limiting middleware (e.g., graphql-depth-limit) into the GraphQL handler to reject queries exceeding a configurable depth (e.g., 8). This prevents maliciously crafted deep queries from exhausting CPU and memory, mitigating DoS attacks.
acceptance: Requests with query depth > 8 receive a 400 response with an error message.
Normal queries (depth ≤ 8) continue to work unchanged.
Performance tests show no noticeable latency increase for valid queries.

tasks.title: Implement refresh‑token rotation and revocation list
tasks.description: Modify the authentication flow to issue a short‑lived access token and a refresh token that is stored hashed in the database. On each token refresh, invalidate the previous refresh token and store the new one, adding the old token to a revocation list. This mitigates token replay and stolen‑token attacks.
acceptance: Refresh endpoint returns a new access token and a new refresh token.
Using an old refresh token after rotation results in a 401 error.
Revoked tokens are persisted and checked on each refresh request.
